## The question

[Center figure which spans over whole page](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/6268/center-figure-which-spans-over-whole-page), asked by [Douglass](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/2198/douglass) on TeX Stack Exchange (2010-11-30; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> I would like to get this to center with 5pt margins on left, right, and top.
> So the picture will cover nearly the whole page with room at the bottom for captions.
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
> \usepackage{tikz}
> \usepackage{caption}
>
> \begin{document}
> \begin{centering}
> \begin{figure}[ht]
>
>
> \begin{tikzpicture}[scale=(3/10)]
>
>   \draw[help lines] (0,0) grid (600mm,500mm);
>
> \end{tikzpicture}
>
> \caption{some caption here}
> \end{figure}
> \clearpage
> \end{centering}
> \end{document}
> ```
:::

It's not centering because your tikzpicture is wider than than the text width, resulting in an overfull `\hbox`.  You can use the `geometry` package to change the margins.
